title: Converting Units in Multistep Problems
short: Change units within a system to solve a problem.

blocks.html: In Grade 4 you converted larger units to smaller ones, like feet to inches. Metric units are built on powers of ten, so converting them is a matter of moving digits.

Going from a bigger unit to a smaller one, multiply: there will be more of the small units. Going from a smaller unit to a bigger one, divide. In a problem with two units, change to one unit before you calculate.

One meter is 100 centimeters, so 3 meters is 3 groups of 100 centimeters: $3 \times 100 = 300$. Going back, 300 centimeters holds 100 centimeters 3 times: $300 \div 100 = 3$. The amount never changes; only the size of the unit you count with changes.

blocks.title: Two steps
blocks.q: A 3 m ribbon is cut into pieces 25 cm long. How many pieces?

blocks.title: Into a bigger unit
blocks.q: Six packages each weigh 12 ounces. How many pounds is that?

blocks.html: Mixing units, such as dividing 3 (meters) by 25 (centimeters). The numbers must count the same unit first. Check: a 3-meter ribbon is long, so there should be quite a few 25-centimeter pieces, not a fraction of one.
